title: Discount depth → units sold
teaser: An amount, not a yes/no; slow sellers got deeper cuts; diminishing returns.
question: How many more units do we sell for each extra point of discount?
ask: Finance wants to know where deeper discounts stop paying off.
sme: a category manager at a grocery chain

variables.name: baseline_units
variables.meaning: average weekly units over the previous 8 weeks

hidden.name: U_trend
hidden.label: a product going out of fashion

post_treatment.name: stockout_flag
post_treatment.meaning: 1 = ran out of stock that week

notes.text: Category managers put deeper discounts on items that were selling slowly.
The regular price is what the shelf label shows outside promotions.
We often match competitor promotions, but we don't keep a record of which weeks competitors ran them.

traps.name: Reverse causation
traps.text: Slow sellers got deeper discounts; ignoring baseline sales makes discounts look useless.

traps.name: Diminishing returns
traps.text: The effect curves; a straight line overstates deep discounts.

traps.name: Unrecorded fading demand
traps.text: Products going out of fashion get deeper discounts and sell less anyway.

traps.name: Unrecorded competitor promotions
traps.text: Matching competitor promotions drives deeper discounts and lower sales; not answerable from this file.
